cur:objects-cross-of-mathilde-essen.summary: The gilt-bronze body of the crucified Christ hangs at the centre of this jewelled processional cross, his arms outstretched across a field of gold, gems and pearls. On the stem a small enamel shows Abbess Mathilde as donor, kneeling before the Virgin and Child. The crucifix itself contains cavities for relics, making the image of Christ also a reliquary.
facts: Wikipedia notes that it was made between about 1000 and 1058, perhaps in stages, and that the corpus may be a later replacement; the reverse bears a punched Agnus Dei with the evangelist symbols.
It forms a group with the Cross of Otto and Mathilde, the Senkschmelz Cross and the Cross of Theophanu, all made for Essen Abbey.
cur:objects-cross-of-mathilde-essen.notes: Dating straddles the year 1000; included because it was begun under Mathilde (d. 1011).

princeton:33876.summary: On this worn bone plaque Christ, with a large halo, stands at the left and reaches toward the face of a smaller figure beside him, the blind man whose eyes he heals. At the right edge a tall structure with a lattice roof survives from the next scene, the tomb of Lazarus. Plaques like this, pierced for attachment, were probably mounted together to tell the miracles of Christ in sequence.
facts: Princeton records the plaque as possibly Roman or Byzantine, made in Syria or south-eastern Turkey in the 9th–11th century; it measures 9.6 × 8 cm.
It was given in 1994 by Bruce Willsie (Class of 1986) together with the plaque of the Raising of Jairus's daughter (y1994-74), which has consecutive accession numbers.
princeton:33876.notes: Whether the two Willsie plaques come from the same object is not stated by the museum.
